scope_approval: Owner instruction in the working session on 2026-09-26: 'Approve narrow release scope — Palace benchmark + QuTiP fixed-point bundle only, openEMS/geometry explicitly unsupported'. A session statement; repository files cannot prove it.
release_actions_approved: none: no tag, publication, merge or pull request is approved by the scope approval
file_class: proprietary QMHP-CEM documentation/data; contains no third-party content
freeze_rule: This file is frozen. tests/test_release_registers.py pins its sha256. It is never edited: a correction is a new, dated, superseding register that names this one.
measurement_rule: Every digest and structured fact here was measured from the git objects of the frozen commit, not copied from another document. Line numbers are at the frozen commit.

tree_binding.rule: A sha256_at_frozen_commit or register_sha256 on a path under one of these prefixes must still match the working tree; tests/test_release_registers.py fails closed otherwise. Digests of other cited files (for example pyproject.toml, uv.lock, orchestrator/manifest.py) are recorded at the frozen commit only: those files may change later, and this register then describes the frozen commit, not the later tree. Each exact_file_sets directory must hold exactly the listed files, so that, for example, a second attempt ledger cannot appear beside the one spent attempt, and no file can be added to the openEMS or geometry directories. Every file in those three directories, and docker/openems.Dockerfile, is digest-bound (REL-BD-01 to REL-BD-03), and the test exercises the registry-resolved openEMS adapter and the package-level planar cells, so a change there fails the test until a superseding scope is approved. An implementation placed in some other directory is not detected by this mechanism.

disposition_vocabulary.QUARANTINED: A record kept exactly as executed with no execution-time register; its files are content-pinned by tests/test_frozen_evidence.py.
disposition_vocabulary.APPROVED-BY-OWNER: An exception or deviation the owner approved in the working session (a session statement the records reference by identifier and digest). It is carried, not removed.
disposition_vocabulary.DISCLOSED-UNRESOLVED: A known defect, gap or ambiguity, disclosed and not fixed in this release.
disposition_vocabulary.IMMUTABLE-TEXT: Stale or incorrect text inside hash-pinned bytes or an executed record. It must not be edited; the dated addendum states how to read it.
disposition_vocabulary.NOT-RECOMPUTABLE: Cannot be established from the repository.
disposition_vocabulary.HUMAN-DECISION-REQUIRED: Needs an owner, reviewer or legal decision; no conclusion is drawn here.
disposition_vocabulary.UNSUPPORTED: Belongs to a capability the release does not support.
disposition_vocabulary.DISCLOSURE: An event disclosed for completeness; no defect in the evidence.

exceptions.title: PALACE-VERIFY-20260915T063014Z: failed execution with no register
exceptions.statement: The record has no manifest.sha256. Its only run, ladder-L1, is RUN_FAILED: Palace exited 1 with 'InterpolationOperator class requires MFEM_USE_GSLIB!' on image 732526ec (no palace-gslib label). Report rendering then failed, so neither report.md nor a manifest was written. summary.json has complete false and verdict fields mesh INCOMPLETE, aux BLOCKED, Object 001 BLOCKED.
exceptions.consequence: Its verdict fields are artefacts of an aborted run and are never counted. Integrity rests on content pins taken at commit time, not on an execution-time register.
exceptions.resolution_route: None. Writing a manifest now is prohibited (it would be an operator register written after the run).

exceptions.title: Residual byte-pattern variability in golden solver output
exceptions.statement: Two eig.csv and error-indicators.csv byte patterns occur across the 13 golden records. The eig.csv patterns differ in Im(f), Q and the error columns at about the 6th significant digit of those columns, and the real parts are identical. error-indicators.csv differs more: its Maximum column differs at the 4th significant digit (1.025941020e-03 against 1.023900419e-03, a relative difference of about 2e-3). The same 10/3 split, on the same three records (025408Z, 063105Z, 233133Z), also occurs in output that takes no Palace input: quantum_results.json (94c4450c... against aefeb606...), gate_report.json (8e272ab7... against e686b849...) and the COLLISION measured value (98.41316039467607 against 98.41316039466896 MHz). Those come from the host-side dressed_system.dressed_spectrum() of the nominal device model, whose pulls differ by up to 7.2e-11 MHz (sink pull 8.72116588454297 against 8.721165884614912). All 13 records carry the same recorded os, python version and dependency lock. The pattern recurred after the thread pin and does not follow the image ID. The three da6f7d0d records are also the three shortest Palace runs (a correlation, not a cause).
exceptions.consequence: Reproducibility is claimed at the level of frequencies and verdicts only (REL-PAL-04). The records show that the splits coincide, not that they share a cause.
exceptions.resolution_route: Root cause not established; would need a separately approved investigation.

exceptions.title: Thread pin not verifiable from the records
exceptions.statement: No Palace record contains OMP_NUM_THREADS or OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS. The pin is declared in docker/palace.Dockerfile only, and each record was built from its own commit's Dockerfile. After the pin, Palace Total still spans 23.207766373 s to 40.952382498 s.
exceptions.consequence: The thread configuration of each run is an expected configuration, not a measured one.
exceptions.resolution_route: None for the existing records.

exceptions.title: Palace image is not registry-pinned
exceptions.statement: 7 distinct local image IDs occur across the 17 Palace records; repo_digest is null in every record; the palace-gslib label is absent on cc87ec6b, 484073ba and 732526ec and 'ON' on the others. The images are not retained in the repository, and a rebuild is not guaranteed bit-identical.
exceptions.consequence: Re-execution on the identical binary cannot be done from the repository alone.
exceptions.resolution_route: A future registry-pinned image; not part of this release.

exceptions.title: Benchmark thresholds are ENGINEERING-RULEs
exceptions.statement: Every Palace threshold (golden tolerance 0.02, expected deviation 1e-4, eigen and backward-error tolerances 1e-6, mesh-refinement 1e-4 rules, height rules, the 400000-DOF budget, timeouts) is an ENGINEERING-RULE of the adapter or campaign, declared before the runs.
exceptions.consequence: No PASS against these rules is a physical-validation statement.
exceptions.resolution_route: None needed; carried as a qualification.

The campaign digest does not bind the analysis code. No separate correction record exists; commit 90924c1 reports a campaign workflow step failure although summary.json has complete true.
exceptions.consequence: 065055Z is kept as executed; its verdicts are superseded in reading only by the later records.
exceptions.resolution_route: A correction record, if the owner wants one; not part of this release.

exceptions.title: campaign.sha256 is a definition digest, not a file manifest, and is unpinned
exceptions.statement: campaign.sha256 holds the canonical-JSON digest 249e1a12... labelled campaign.json; sha256sum -c against the file bytes (ef3689ac...) would fail. The .sha256 suffix is outside the membership rule and no pin covers it (file sha256 d0d2d5a6... in all four VERIFY records).

exceptions.title: Licence status of the tools that produced the Palace evidence is not recorded
exceptions.statement: Palace 0.13.0 (commit a61c8cbe) produced the Palace records, with the libraries its image builds through Palace's superbuild (docker/palace.Dockerfile names MFEM, hypre, METIS, PETSc/SLEPc, SuperLU_DIST and libCEED 'and the rest', and enables GSLIB) and the Ubuntu runtime packages it installs (OpenMPI, OpenBLAS and the GCC runtime libraries, among others). gmsh (4.15.2 in uv.lock, via the optional 'palace' extra) generated the committed meshes. That component list is not exhaustive and no component version other than Palace's and gmsh's was measured. The release registers record no licence or distribution status for them. The repository LICENSE says third-party software such as Palace and MFEM is governed by its own licences.
exceptions.consequence: No legal conclusion is drawn here (CLAUDE.md section 12).
exceptions.resolution_route: Human or legal review before any publication.

exceptions.title: Resource-limit deviation: memory_limit_MB = 1024 not enforced
exceptions.statement: macOS rejected RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA of 1 GiB (errno 22 EINVAL, reproduced by the dummy diagnostic). For RLIMIT_AS the diagnostic ties this to virtual size: the smallest accepted soft limit on its ladder was 512 GiB against a 415.10 GiB process; the cause of the RLIMIT_DATA rejection was not measured. The execution used the separately approved rule QUTIP-A-MACOS-AS-GROWTH-LIMIT-v1: RLIMIT_AS soft = hard = the checker's baseline VSZ + 1073741824 bytes, an ADDRESS-SPACE GROWTH LIMIT. The frozen-rules file was not edited.
exceptions.consequence: Protocol conformance is QUALIFIED: RESOURCE-LIMIT DEVIATION (REL-QT-01, REL-QT-06). The growth control is not a total-memory or resident-memory limit; memory committed later inside regions reserved before the limit is not established as bounded; child processes inherit the absolute RLIMIT_AS.
exceptions.resolution_route: Carried permanently for this execution. It is never to be described as a 1 GiB total-memory limit (that description is not correct).

exceptions.title: Launcher-registered records and the narrow file-type exception
exceptions.statement: The four QUTIP-A records use their writers' own sha256sum-format registers (launcher-manifest.sha256, SHA256SUMS, qualification-manifest.sha256), not manifest.sha256. They contain 48 files whose suffixes are outside orchestrator.manifest.COMMITTABLE_SUFFIXES (.py, .stdout, .stderr, .log, run-attempt1.* timing files, PRESERVATION-SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS). None contains a NUL byte; the four records total 1195866 bytes. The owner approved this as a NARROW RECORD-SPECIFIC EXCEPTION on 2026-09-26; the general policy is unchanged.
exceptions.consequence: scripts/check_record_files.py would flag these files if run on the records without --allow; no CLI command verifies these registers (EXC-R05).
exceptions.resolution_route: None; the exception is record-specific and does not extend to any other record.

exceptions.statement: The first launcher stopped at BLOCKED-PREFLIGHT because it could not apply its fixed memory cap; its message ends '(SubprocessError: Exception occurred in preexec_fn.)'. The run then proceeded through a diagnostic, a revised launcher, a new resource-rule approval and a new execution approval (-v2).

exceptions.resolution_route: None needed.

exceptions.title: Stale status text in hash-pinned bridge files and inside the evidence
exceptions.statement: The protocol document, checker, exporter, schema and launcher still say they are prepared, not approved and not executed, or that the resource rule is PROPOSED. Their bytes are pinned by the executed record, and tests/test_qutip_bridge_contract.py asserts three of the strings. The snapshot inside the evidence carries 'PROPOSED ENGINEERING-RULE, not approved' and the preservation README says 'No QuTiP calculation has been run.', both true when written. The execution record's launcher-final.json and attempt-receipt.json embed the rule text and rule_status 'PROPOSED; requires separate human approval before scientific execution' verbatim, although both also record the approval file the launcher consumed (resource_rule_approval: OWNER-APPROVAL-2026-09-26-QUTIP-A-AS-GROWTH-RULE-v1, sha256 7d38e9de..., equal to RESOURCE-RULE-APPROVAL.json). The qualification record's qualification-final.json carries the same PROPOSED text, which was accurate when written: the approval file names that file's digest (63efd145...), so it was written afterwards. The owner's approval itself is a session statement (REL-QT-10). The byte-identical checker and schema copies inside the three QUTIP-A records carry the same status text as the repository files.

exceptions.title: No CLI verifier for the launcher-registered or quarantined records
exceptions.statement: `cem verify-results` re-hashes a record against its manifest.sha256, so it covers the 16 manifested Palace records (palace-golden.yml runs it on each new golden record). It cannot verify the four launcher-registered QUTIP-A records or the quarantined 063014Z as records, because none has a root-level manifest.sha256; it can verify only nested subtrees that carry one (the execution record's checker-output/, and the copied export archive directory inside three QUTIP-A records). `cem report` also needs batch_report.json, which no PALACE-* record has. Those five records are verified as whole records only by tests/test_frozen_evidence.py.
exceptions.consequence: The verifier that covers every in-scope record is `pytest tests/test_frozen_evidence.py`.
exceptions.resolution_route: A CLI change would be a separate approved change.

exceptions.title: Enforcement limits of the evidence controls
exceptions.statement: Frozen-evidence enforcement is file immutability, not evidence governance; the promotion guard declines PALACE-VERIFY and PALACE-GOLDEN, so nothing mechanically judges their verdicts; several contract clauses are behavioural only. Pre-push secret scanning does not protect a clone that never installed it, --no-verify, other routes to the remote, or history already pushed, and zero findings means only that no rule matched.
exceptions.consequence: The registers are frozen by a digest test (tests/test_release_registers.py); their content is a human-reviewed reading, not a mechanical verdict.
exceptions.resolution_route: None in this release.
